prompt: Stage 4-5, level 8, 66 gold, 44 HP. This is your planned rolldown for two 1-star 4-costs (tank and carry). Your bench holds three units that are not in the comp. Put the rolldown steps in the order a disciplined player executes them.

steps: Decide the stop conditions before touching the shop: both targets 2-starred, or a gold floor of 10, whichever comes first
Sell the three off-comp bench units so every shop copy you hit has a slot to land in
Roll, buying every copy of both targets on sight, and also buy any 4-cost that would upgrade the weakest board slot
When a stop condition triggers, stop immediately and re-position the new 2-stars before the timer ends

explanation:
The stop condition is set first because once you are pressing D you will not set it honestly: at 18 gold with one target hit, the pull to "just three more" is exactly how a 66-gold rolldown becomes a 0-gold rolldown that leaves you at level 8 with no interest at 5-1. Clearing the bench is next and it is the step Emerald players skip: with three dead units on the bench you have six slots, and a shop that shows two copies of your carry and a useful 4-cost needs three. A missed copy because the bench was full is the most expensive mistake in the whole sequence.

Rolling comes third, and "buy any 4-cost that upgrades the weakest slot" is part of the same step because the point of the rolldown is board strength, not the specific names you wrote down. Re-positioning is last and it is not optional: a freshly 2-starred tank sitting where the 1-star was is often in the wrong hex for the new opponent, and the timer will not wait.
principle: Set the floor and the stop before you press D; after that the shop makes the decisions for you.
commonMistake: Rolling with a full bench, then selling in a panic mid-rolldown and missing the copy that was in the shop you just refreshed.
